Hi Hannah / team,

Thanks for the draft order form and attached SLA. Our legal and platform teams worked through the doc and weve captured the highest-priority redlines in the attached PDF (summary below). We want to keep timeline tight because procurement needs the PO by end of next week.

Top items from Starlite:
- Uptime target: your draft calls for 99.95% monthly. Starlite requires 99.9% for the hosted tier and 99.95% for Dedicated. Please propose a table to reflect both.
- Service credits: request a linear credits table with lower cap (max 20% of monthly fees) and payment within 30 days.
- Response times: require P1 acknowledgement within 15 minutes, P1 remediation SLA of 4 hours for Dedicated vs 8 hours for hosted.
- Maintenance windows: we need a carveout for scheduled upgrades during regional blackout periods; request 14-day notice for major upgrades and a weekly 2am-5am maintenance window for non-critical updates.
- Measurement: please confirm the metric (regional-monthly availability vs global aggregated) and include error-budget definition.

Weve also attached a short redline PDF and a separate list of attachments well need as part of SOC2 evidence.

Can you confirm Redwood legal can review our redlines and come back with tracked changes by Thursday 5/28? Procurement will need a final DocuSign link by Friday.

Thanks,
Leah

Leah — thanks for the clear summary and the redline PDF. Attaching our internal tracker (Starlite_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx) with an ops + legal proposal. High level responses below so were all aligned before Lauren does formal redlines: 

Summary of Redwood proposals (see attached for tracked changes):
- Availability: propose a two-tier table: Hosted: 99.9% (base) with a Gold add-on at 99.95%; Dedicated: 99.95. Were open to a narrow middle ground if Starlite has firm constraints.
- Credits: well cap credits at 25% of monthly bill for an outage month; payments net 45 days to match our billing cadence. We can consider 30 days if procurement requires.
- Response times: agree on separate ladders for Hosted vs Dedicated. Suggest P1 ack within 15 min, remediation target 6 hours (hosted) / 4 hours (dedicated). 6 hours gives us reasonable on-call runway for routing/fallbacks.
- Maintenance: propose standard maintenance exclusion of up to 6 hours per week (local time), and 72-hour notice for routine upgrades; for major platform upgrades propose 30-day notice and a maximum of 12 hours planned blackout per quarter. Emergency maintenance will continue to be excluded but will require post-event notification and root cause.
- Measurement: Redwood measures at region-level (traffic-weighted) and reports monthly uptime percentage with supporting trace logs. We will include the error budget formula in the order form.

Open ops/legal asks for Redwood: 
- Lauren: can you take the attached and produce tracked-change redlines focusing on legal language around carveouts, credit calculation, and measurement?
- Dev: can you confirm whether the 6-hour weekly window for non-critical updates is operationally feasible for hosted customers in us-west and eu-west regions?

Attachments: Starlite_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx (contains proposed wording + credit table)
SLA_TRACKER.xlsx (ops impact matrix - will send in next message)

Proposed next steps: Lauren to return redlines Thu 5/28 EOD -> then Leah/legal to counter or accept -> DocuSign agreed by Fri 5/29. Let me know if anyone needs an earlier call.

Best,
Hannah

On Tue, May 25, 2026 at 11:38 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Leah — thanks for the clear summary and the redline PDF. Attaching our internal tracker ...

Thanks — I reviewed Hannah's draft and produced tracked changes on Starlite_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx. Im sending a short note of the legal positions so procurement has visibility: 

Legal highlights / required edits:
- Measurement definition: must define "monthly uptime percentage" precisely (numerator = total regional available seconds; denominator = total regional seconds in month minus scheduled maintenance window seconds). Also require Redwood to provide exportable telemetry for audit requests.
- Credits cap: propose cap at 25% (Redwoods number) but require a minimum payout window of 30 days from determination (we can agree to 45 days invoicing, but contract should not exceed 60 days net).
- Force majeure / platform upgrade carveout: remove language that gives Redwood broad discretion to declare a platform upgrade an "exclusion". Replace with narrowly-tailored language: Redwood must notify 30 calendar days for non-emergency platform upgrades that impact availability and offer a rolling fallback plan.
- Emergency maintenance: require post-event RCA within 10 business days.
- Metrics and aggregation: prefer region-level availability with per-region credits rather than global aggregation; will accept global aggregation for Dedicated only.

Ops question (Dev): the 6-hour weekly window — we need to ensure customers can opt-in/out and that the contract reflects the local timezone. If ops confirms feasibility, legal will keep the clause but add explicit timezone & opt-out language.

I attached SLA_TRACKER.xlsx with the legal comments tab populated. Once Hannah confirms small wording tweaks, I will send the file back to Starlite as tracked changes.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com

Hannah / Lauren — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear positions. We reviewed the tracked changes and are broadly aligned on the structure. A few points from Starlite to close the loop: 

- Availability table: Starlite accepts the two-tier approach. Well sign for Hosted @ 99.9% but would like a specific addendum to convert to 99.95% if we commit to an annual reserved capacity minimum. Please add a short clause describing conversion mechanics.
- Credits timing: Starlite can accept 45-day payment timing for credits, provided the cap remains 25% and the method of calculation is exactly the numerator/denominator Lauren proposed.
- Platform upgrade notice: we can accept 30-day notice for non-emergency upgrades. For urgent security patches that may require shorter notice, we ask that Redwood provide a mitigation plan and post-incident RCA within 7 business days.
- Maintenance windows: Starlite cannot accept a rolling 6-hour weekly blackout for Hosted without the ability to opt-out for high-traffic periods. We propose an opt-out clause with no more than 6 opt-out days per calendar quarter.

Procurement note: attaching PO routing instructions. Wed like a DocuSign link once legal exchanges finish. Here is our DocuSign envelope request: https://www.docusign.com/uas/Signing/1234abcd-starlite-orderform.

Next steps: Lauren to incorporate the small change on conversion mechanics and the opt-out days language; Hannah to send final tracked doc by EOD Fri 5/29 so procurement can complete the PO and signature next week.

Appreciate the fast cadence — happy to jump on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Leah
Starlite Analytics
